title: Denny Seiwell quits Wings | 1973
content:
Wings’ original drummer Denny Seiwell quit the band on 29 August 1973.

He had been due to fly to Lagos in Nigeria the next day to record the band’s third album, but had grown disenchanted with the low wage of £70 a week he and the other non-McCartney members of the group were earning. His decision to leave was spurred on by the departure of guitarist Henry McCullough earlier in the month, and the knowledge that he could resume a lucrative career as a session drummer.

Seiwell had unsuccessfully tried to persuade Paul McCartney to postpone the imminent Band On The Run recording sessions in Lagos.

I picked up the phone and called Paul, and I said, ‘I’m done. I can’t do this anymore.’ It was hard to do, really, extremely hard to do. And he was shocked.
Denny Seiwell, 2016
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 1: 1969-73

The phone call between the two men was heated, and ended with McCartney slamming down the phone. Minutes later Seiwell’s phone rang again, and he heard Linda McCartney exclaiming: “How dare you inconvenience us?”

Seiwell shot back that he had given up a good career in New York to earn relatively little for three years. “I don’t want to hear this,” he told her, and hung up.

Denny Laine and engineer Geoff Emerick had flown out to Lagos earlier that day, and the McCartneys followed the next day.
